text: Chapter 7 introduces the systematic study of 3-part chords organized across 840 voicings, emphasizing their practical importance in guitar playing (spanning pages 66-100). The chapter establishes that 3-part chords are easier to play than 4-part chords, making them a foundational priority for guitarists building chord literacy. By cataloging and demonstrating these variations, the chapter equips players with a comprehensive chord vocabulary grounded in the specific ergonomic constraints and affordances of the fretboard. This systematic approach to 3-part chord voicings forms the first installment of a deeper exploration into chord construction and application.
